quiz.q: Why is the status of the Buddha as a political philosopher considered contested in political thought?
options: Buddhism focuses on otherworldly salvation, yet historical rulers sought Buddha's counsel on governance.
Buddha established a powerful territorial empire, yet refused to draft formal administrative edicts.
Buddhism advocated hereditary monarchical rule, yet completely rejected the institution of private property.
Buddha authored comprehensive military manuals, yet preached complete non-violence in all external relations.
quiz.why: The notes explain that while Buddhism is an otherworldly religion, kings regularly sought Buddha's advice on good governance.

quiz.q: How does the Buddhist conception of the social contract differ from the ancient Hindu tradition?
options: The Buddhist contract is between Man and God, whereas the Hindu contract is formed among men.
The Buddhist contract is formed among men, whereas the Hindu contract is between Man and God.
The Buddhist contract establishes hereditary divine rule, whereas the Hindu tradition relies on republican elections.
The Buddhist contract is mediated by priests, whereas the Hindu tradition rejects political agreements entirely.
quiz.why: In Buddhist thought, the social contract is a human agreement among men, whereas Hindu tradition conceives it as between Man and God.

quiz.q: How does the Buddhist ideal of the 'World Monarch' differ from the Hindu 'Chakravarty Samrat'?
options: The World Monarch acquires territory through force, while the Chakravarty Samrat rules primarily through love.
The World Monarch relies on divine decree, while the Chakravarty Samrat governs through republican consensus.
The World Monarch wins hearts through love, whereas the Chakravarty Samrat acquires land through force.
The World Monarch wields the chariot wheel, whereas the Chakravarty Samrat turns the Dhamma wheel.
quiz.why: The notes specify that the Hindu Chakravarty Samrat acquires land through force, whereas the Buddhist World Monarch wins hearts through love.

quiz.q: Why is the ancient Buddhist Sangha considered an early example of deliberative democracy?
options: It restricted institutional membership exclusively to noble rulers who debated regional diplomatic peace treaties.
It reserved legislative policy decisions for an appointed council of hereditary high priests and scholars.
It appointed an absolute executive leader whose administrative decrees were accepted without any collective debate.
It made decisions through open debate while practicing equality across social caste and gender divisions.
quiz.why: The Buddhist Sangha functioned as a deliberative democracy by debating matters collectively and rejecting caste and gender hierarchies.
